title: Same Numbers, Different Word Problems
intro: Help your student see why the same numbers can require different operations.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Read the paired stories together and label what each number means in each story. Compare the unknowns before calculating.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Story A: Alex has 12 books. Maya brings 4 more. How many books are there altogether?

12 + 4 = 16

Story B: After Maya brings 4 books, the class has 12. How many books were there before?

12 − 4 = 8

Ask your student

What changes between the two questions even though the numbers stay the same?

If your student needs help

If the student copies the first operation, ask them to retell the second story in order.
